lesson_title: The Flat Rope That Isn't Empty: Pulses and Superposition
hook_text: Two pulses collide, the rope goes perfectly flat — and then BOTH come back from nowhere.
clip_script: Flick a rope up on your side. Your friend flicks theirs down, exactly the same size, at exactly the same moment. A hump races one way, a dip races the other. They meet in the middle — and the rope goes perfectly, completely flat. Gone? Watch. A heartbeat later the hump pops out one side and the dip pops out the other, both full size, both still travelling, as if nothing happened. Here is the secret: the rope adds heights like money. Plus 25 and minus 25 is zero — but zero displacement is not zero energy. At that flat instant, all the energy is hiding in the motion of the rope, like a swing at the bottom of its arc: lowest point, highest speed. That is the principle of superposition. Same signs build a giant — constructive. Opposite signs cancel — destructive. And after every meeting, every pulse walks away unchanged. The exam will show you the flat rope and ask where the pulses went. Now you know: nowhere. They are passing straight through.
visual_style: A rope stretched across the frame in bold colour; a glowing crest and a glowing trough sweep toward each other, cancel to a flat line that pulses with hidden energy, then re-emerge; signed numbers float and add above the meeting point.
mood: A magic trick that turns out to be honest bookkeeping.
pacing: Build toward the collision, a held beat on the flat rope, snap reveal of the reappearing pulses, brisk rule recap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never lose marks on an interference diagram again.
